citations.quote: “Personal Information” means any information that directly or indirectly identifies an eBay User that you obtain or send to eBay through your participation in the Program and your use of the Developer Tools, including information that you collect or receive, or have access to, directly from Your Users in connection with your Application, information that is included in eBay Content, or information that you otherwise receive from eBay about Your Users or other eBay Users and their trading activities.

citations.clause: Section 9 (Protecting User Privacy), Collecting and Storing Personal Information
citations.quote: You agree to promptly delete Personal Information on the earlier of: (i) when required by your data privacy and data retention policies; (ii) when requested by eBay or by the applicable eBay User to whom the Personal Information pertains, (iii) when the Personal Information is no longer necessary for the specific, legitimate purpose for which it was collected or processed for your Application, or (iv) when your participation in the Program is terminated.

You must destroy all copies of, or anything containing, eBay Content and Personal Information in your possession within ten (10) days after termination, and you will provide written certification of destruction to eBay upon eBay’s request.

dispositions.ownerDecision: Owner decision, not provider evidence: eBay-issued offer and listing identifiers stored against a seller are classified as Personal Information under the Section 1 definition, because they are received from eBay through the Program and indirectly identify an eBay User. eBay has not been asked to confirm this and the conservative reading is deliberate. If eBay later states these identifiers are not Personal Information, the only cost of this choice is a deleted column nobody was reading.

Reports only include paid transactions where we are able to collect payment from the customer (view Schedule 2 of your Apple Developer Agreement).

For In-App Purchases made using alternative payment processing or linking out to a webpage, you're responsible for taxes, including (but not limited to): Determining if a transaction is taxable; Charging and collecting the taxes at the applicable rate; Remitting the taxes to the appropriate taxing authority.
A UUID you create at the time of purchase that associates the transaction with a customer on your own service.
Deleting customers through the RevenueCat dashboard or API clears out all of their data and is sufficient for GDPR erasure requests.
Deleting a customer will also remove all their purchase history for sandbox and production data
there will be only one App User ID within the original_app_user_id field

dispositions.ownerDecision: Owner decision, not provider evidence, on three points. First, SnapList's Apple and RevenueCat references are an entitlement mapping, not a tax record: the stored rows carry a Clerk user id, a RevenueCat app user id, an Apple original transaction id, and allowance state, and carry no customer identity, price, or tax amount. Apple never discloses the customer to the developer; the only per-customer link is a UUID the developer itself creates. So the row is deleted at account erasure rather than retained for a fixed number of years, and the 7-year fallback is deliberately not used. This conclusion has not been reviewed by a tax professional. Second, one RevenueCat customer is the original_app_user_id plus its aliases array, so deleting the customer deletes the whole alias set; that follows from the two cited clauses read together rather than from a single sentence stating it. Third, RevenueCat's public documentation does not state that deletion is synchronous, so completion requires reading the customer back rather than trusting the delete response. If SnapList ever adopts alternative payment processing or external purchase links, Apple stops collecting the tax and this row must be reopened.
